candidates.original_title: Action anticipation through attribution of false belief by 2-year-olds
candidates.description: Anticipatory-looking false-belief task with two false-belief conditions (False Belief 1 and False Belief 2), measuring differential looking score to belief-congruent vs belief-incongruent locations
candidates.citation_sentence: In the original studies of [37] and [34], the main finding was that participants generally showed more anticipatory looking to the belief-congruent than to the belief-incongruent location, with no significant differences between the False Belief 1 and False Belief 2 conditions.
candidates.notes: Cited [37] as primary original; [34] also contributed to this paradigm. Overall original findings not replicated; only False Belief 1 condition showed a significant effect

candidates.original_title: Action anticipation through attribution of false belief by 2-year-olds
candidates.description: Participants should look proportionally more toward the belief-congruent than the belief-incongruent location in a false-belief anticipatory-looking task.
candidates.citation_sentence: In the original studies of [37] and [34], the main finding was that participants generally showed more anticipatory looking to the belief-congruent than to the belief-incongruent location, with no significant differences between the False Belief 1 and False Belief 2 conditions.
candidates.notes: The combined replication of the paradigm showed no overall significant effect; the two false-belief conditions went in opposite directions.
